chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever seeks livelihood in this world in order to be self-sufficient from people, to expand (sustenance) upon his family, and to show kindness to his neighbor, will meet God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, and his face will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.

key_terms.اسْتِعْفَاف: Self-sufficiency, abstaining from asking others; a virtue of preserving one's honor and dignity
key_terms.الرِّزْق: Livelihood, daily sustenance, provision — includes both material earning and the spiritual dimension of God's provision
key_terms.تَعَطُّف: Showing tenderness, kindness, or compassion, especially to neighbors
key_terms.تَوْسِيع: Expanding or increasing provision for one's household
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: A divine epithet meaning Mighty and Majestic, used as an honorific for God
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْر: The night of the full moon (14th of the lunar month), the brightest night, used as a metaphor for radiant honor

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on seeking worldly livelihood to support one's family and avoid dependence on others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that seeking worldly livelihood with the right intentions — to avoid dependence on others, provide generously for one's family, and assist one's neighbors — is a spiritually meritorious act. The reward described is remarkable: such a person will meet God on the Day of Judgment with a face radiantly bright like the full moon. This hadith challenges any notion that worldly work is spiritually inferior, affirming instead that honest labor with noble intentions is a form of worship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who seeks the livelihood in the world would be needless from the people, and would expand (sustenance) upon his family, and be helpful upon his neighbours, and would meet Allah<sup>azwj</sup> on the Day of Judgement and his face would be like the moon on the night of the full moon’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

one who works to earn his sustenance in this world so he would not need to spread his hands before people for help, to better the living conditions of his family and to show kindness to his neighbors will, on the Judgment Day, go before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, with his face as bright as the full moon.’”
